title: GDExtension: `virtual_method_list` is still modified without synchronization in `_gdvirtual_init_method_ptr` (follow-up to #120796)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in a custom **4.6.stable** build (`89cea143987d564363e15d207438530651d943ac`) — that is where we hit the related crash fixed by #120796.
- The code described here is **still present in master** (`2f2a9f4cc6`), `core/object/object.cpp`.

### System information

Linux 7.0 (Ubuntu), Godot 4.6.stable custom editor build (`target=editor debug_symbols=yes`) with the `godot_voxel` module, AMD RX 9070 / RADV. The problem is code-level and platform independent.

### Issue description

**How this was found:** we came to this function for a different reason — we were hitting the crash
that #120796 fixed, in a project that uses a GDExtension `VoxelGeneratorScript` subclass. While
backporting that fix to our 4.6 build and reading the surrounding code, we noticed that the *same*
function still contains an unsynchronized section. So this is not a bug we set out to look for; it
is one that became visible because of the other one. We have not observed it in the wild — see the
honesty note at the end of "How we ran into this area".

#120796 fixed the transient `nullptr` store in `Object::_gdvirtual_init_method_ptr()`, and in doing so established the premise: *several threads can enter that function at once for the same object* — quoting the PR, "TWO THREADS CAN ENTER THIS CONDITION IF THEY BOTH BELIEVE THEY ARE THE FIRST CALLER".

The `TOOLS_ENABLED` block in the same function is still unsynchronized:

```cpp
#ifdef TOOLS_ENABLED
	if (_extension->reloadable) {
		VirtualMethodTracker *tracker = memnew(VirtualMethodTracker);
		tracker->method = (void **)&r_fn_ptr;
		tracker->next = virtual_method_list;   // read
		virtual_method_list = tracker;         // write
	}
#endif
```

Two threads resolving **two different virtual methods of the same object** concurrently both do read-then-write on `virtual_method_list`. That is a lost update: both trackers get the same `next`, and one of them never ends up in the list.

The consequence is worse than a leak. `Object::clear_internal_extension()` walks that list on extension reload and resets every registered pointer:

```cpp
	while (virtual_method_list) {
		(*virtual_method_list->method) = nullptr;
		virtual_method_list = virtual_method_list->next;
	}
```

A tracker lost to the race means **its `_gdvirtual_*` pointer is never reset**. After the extension is reloaded, that member still points into the previous library image, and the next call through it jumps into unmapped or reused memory. Editor-only, non-deterministic, and it surfaces far away from its cause.

### How we ran into this area

We hit the bug fixed by #120796 in a project that uses a GDExtension `VoxelGeneratorScript` subclass: `godot_voxel` calls `_generate_block()` from a dozen worker threads, all resolving the virtual for the first time in the same instant. That gave **4 crashes in 24 launches**, with the null jump exactly as described in #120796:

```
#7  0x0000000000000000 in ?? ()
#8  VoxelGeneratorScript::_gdvirtual__generate_block_call
#9  GenerateBlockTask::run_cpu_generation
```

Backporting the #120796 change gave **0 crashes in 48 launches** — a good independent confirmation
of that fix, from a completely different workload than the glTF one it was reported against.

That measurement is included here only as evidence that the concurrent-first-call situation is real
and easy to hit in practice. The tracker race itself we have **not** observed: we found it by reading
the function while backporting, and the reasoning above is code inspection on top of the concurrency
premise that #120796 already established. Reporting it anyway, because a stale function pointer that
survives a hot reload is exactly the kind of defect that stays invisible during development and
surfaces much later.

### Suggested fix

The slow path runs once per object and method, so a lock costs nothing measurable:

```cpp
void Object::_gdvirtual_init_method_ptr(uint32_t p_compat_hash, void *&r_fn_ptr, const StringName &p_fn_name, bool p_compat) const {
	static Mutex gdvirtual_init_mutex;
	MutexLock lock(gdvirtual_init_mutex);
	if (r_fn_ptr != nullptr) {
		return; // another thread already resolved it; same result
	}
	... // existing resolution, TOOLS_ENABLED tracker, and the final store
}
```

Guarding only the `TOOLS_ENABLED` block would fix the list, but the early-out above also stops N threads from redundantly resolving the same method.

### Steps to reproduce

No minimal reproduction project — the window is small and the observable effect needs an extension reload after a multithreaded first call. It requires an editor build, a `reloadable` GDExtension, at least two of its virtual methods first called from different threads on the same object concurrently, and then a reload of that extension.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A — see above.
